text:
Avery (CEO): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — starting this thread to capture any remaining Qs about strategy, mission, market positioning, and competitors. Ask away and we'll answer live for the next 15 mins.
Priya (Head of Product): Thanks! I'll kick us off — how tightly should product teams bake the Redwood thesis (serving-first) into roadmaps vs. UX features?
Avery (CEO): Short answer: both. The thesis guides tradeoffs (latency/cost/reliability) and prioritization; UX features should be built on top of that so customers get predictable inference.
Sam (Engineering): Curious on tactical guidance — if a feature needs lower latency but higher cost, do we prefer dedicated infra or a cheaper model variant + cache?
Marco (CTO): Depends on SLAs. For customer-facing low-latency SLOs, Dedicated + KV caching. For internal or low-tier apps, fallback to quantized model + aggressive caching. We'll publish decision trees in the playbook.
Jordan (Sales): On positioning — when a prospect asks "how do you compare to cloud vendor X?" what's the 30-sec pitch?
Avery (CEO): Say: we give predictable, economical inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with first-class tooling for rollouts and observability. Emphasize serving guarantees and unit-economics controls.
Priya (Head of Product): Follow-up: competitors that only offer hosted endpoints — call out their strength (simplicity) and weakness (lack of predictable capacity / private deployments).
Taylor (People Ops): Small org question — will this influence hiring priorities for next quarter (more infra vs. product PMs)?
Avery (CEO): Yes — hiring will skew infra/serving engineers and applied ML for quantization and evals in Q2, while also adding 1-2 senior PMs to translate serving capabilities into clear product surfaces.
Sam (Engineering): Any change to roadmap timings? We had some features planned for Hosted API improvements in Q2.
Priya (Head of Product): Hosted API improvements stay but we'll re-prioritize the batching/cache UX epic to land earlier — high leverage for cost-sensitive customers.
Jordan (Sales): Pricing message — are we doubling down on usage-based + reserved capacity? Anything new to tell prospects?
Avery (CEO): Continue both. Highlight committed reserved options for Dedicated and new compliance add-ons for Private. We'll have a short PRD next week with updated pricing bullets.
Sam (Engineering): Regarding competitors who advertise model quality as differentiator — how do we position when customers ask about model accuracy vs. serving?
Marco (CTO): Be honest: model quality matters, but production behavior (latency, tail SLOs, multitenant isolation) determines user experience at scale. Offer to run a short eval harness we maintain to compare real workload metrics.
Priya (Head of Product): I'll drop a template eval + onboarding checklist in #product after this thread.
Avery (CEO): One more — region strategy question: should we push APAC earlier for Dedicated or Private?
Jordan (Sales): Demand in APAC is rising for regulated customers — Private/VPC first, Dedicated afterward.
Priya (Head of Product): We'll include region gating in the roadmap notes.
Sam (Engineering): Quick ops question — will smart routing policies be exposed to customers or remain internal for now?
Marco (CTO): Initial rollout is internal (managed policies) with a customer-facing policy API by end of H2.
Taylor (People Ops): Thanks — great clarity for hiring and org planning.
Avery (CEO): Great thread — we'll synthesize these Qs into the all-hands notes and a short FAQ. If you have follow-ups, ping me or Priya. :raised_hands:
